function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

I don’t have a way to probe your connection from here, so the best thing you can do is run a quick speed‑test yourself. Here are a few easy options: | Method | How to Run | Notes | |--------|------------|-------| | **Web browser** | Go to (or ) and click “Go” | Works on any device with a browser. | | **Command line (Windows)** | Open PowerShell or Command Prompt and type:
`powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sivel/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py -OutFile speedtest.py; python speedtest.py"` | Requires Python installed. | | **Command line (Linux/macOS)** | Open Terminal and type:
`curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sivel/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py > speedtest.py && python3 speedtest.py` | Requires Python 3. | | **Mobile app** | Install the official Speedtest app from Google Play or the App Store. | Gives results for Wi‑Fi and cellular. | If you’re on a Windows machine and want a quick one‑liner without installing anything extra, you can try the built‑in `PowerShell` command below (it downloads the script and runs it): ```powershell powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sivel/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py -OutFile speedtest.py; python speedtest.py" ``` Just paste that into a PowerShell window and hit Enter. It will print out your download/upload speeds and ping. Let me know if you need help interpreting the results or troubleshooting a slow connection!
